newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to raise pensions, sacks director - paper.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to raise pensions, sacks director - paper.

text.p: Croatia is mulling plans to increase monthly pensions by some 22 percent this year, the daily newspaper Vecernji List reported on Saturday.
It also said the government sacked the director of the state-run pension fund (MIORH) on Friday for delaying December pension payments until January 15.
Damir Zoric, who previously headed the Office for Refugees, was appointed to steer MIORH out of the current crisis.
The government follows mass protests by pensioners last November. Aside from Croatia's 200,000 or so refugees and displaced persons, they are the most impoverished citizens.
Living on a meagre 1,000 kuna ($180) net average, including 100 kuna contributed by the government each month, pensioners can hardly make ends meet between each monthly payment.
They were outraged when MIORH said earlier this month it would not be able to pay their pensions until January 20.
Some media reported funds had run dry while the previous chief was on leave, but this was never officially confirmed.
Government spokesmen were not available at the weekend to comment on the newspaper report, but state-run television broadcast much the same information.
Some 25 percent of pensions are paid in the form of mandatory health care contributions into the public health system. According to Vecernji List, this will be reduced to 18 percent.
While not resulting in a lower level of medical services, the cut is designed to free a total of 700 million kuna this year which will be distibuted to pensioners, the paper said.
Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa announced in 1996 the government would launch a much delayed pension reform which would partly privatise the system. But these plans never came to fruition.
